## The short version

**MagSafe** is Apple's own magnetic charging system. **Qi2** is the open industry standard built on it. **Qi2.2** is the faster version of Qi2.

| | Speed | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Qi2** | Up to 15W | Introduced in 2023. It adds a magnetic ring for alignment, which improves efficiency. The design draws on Apple's MagSafe contributions ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey), [WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). |
| **Qi2.2** (also sold as "Qi2 25W") | Up to 25W | Launched July 2025. The WPC says it has nearly 70% more power than Qi2 and can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). |
| **MagSafe** | 15W, or 25W on newer iPhones | Apple's branding and certification. Apple's current MagSafe Charger is certified for Qi2 25W, so it follows the same standard ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8)). |

## Things to watch for

- **Your phone sets the ceiling.** Apple lists 25W for the iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max, 17 series and 18 Pro models. The iPhone 16 and 16 Pro peak at 22.5W, and the iPhone Air at 20W. The iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier top out at 15W ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)). The 16e has no wireless charging at all.
- **"MagSafe-compatible" is not the same as certified.** Macworld says uncertified chargers with magnets are usually just 7.5W, roughly twice as slow ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). Check the Qi2 logo or search the [WPC certified product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).
- **Android support is limited.** The Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold do Qi2 at 15W, and the 10 Pro XL does Qi2.2 at 25W. Samsung's Galaxy S26 line is "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).
- **Power adapter matters.** Apple's charger needs a 30W or higher adapter for 25W, and it doesn't come with one ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)).

## If you want to buy

- [Apple MagSafe Charger (2 m), $49](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8) is certified Qi2 25W.
- [Baseus PicoGo AM52 Qi2.2 power bank](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w) is a portable option. The Verge found it had the fastest wireless charging of the seven batteries it tested. Dealectric lists it at $59.99, or $53.99 with code AM52. This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy.

If you tell me your phone model, I can say whether 25W is worth paying for.
